2.text: the mode of life. They refuse to take the drum and to call the “spirits,”

3.text: leave the amulets in the field, from very fear,¹ etc.

4.text: The parents of young persons “doomed to inspiration” (eñeˊñɪtvu lɪˊnyo)
4.resolved: eñeˊñɪtvu = e, n+U+0303, e, U+02CA, n+U+0303, U+026A, t, v, u; lɪˊnyo = l, U+026A, U+02CA, n, y, o
4.note: Native gloss confirmed at 4× against the raster: dotless ɪ (U+026A) in both ñɪtvu and lɪˊnyo, not r or i as mz/ocr had it (r→ɪ is a known CATMuS substitution). Raised marks after eñe and lɪ are stress U+02CA, not apostrophes, per §4. Checked lexicon lookup for li'nyo: corpus attests lɪˊn˙yo (with palatalization dot on n) on 1-063 only, but this page's crop shows no dot between n and yo at 4× — different reading, keyed as printed, not via that key.

5.text: act differently, according to temperament and family conditions. Sometimes

6.text: they protest against the call coming to their child, and try to induce it to

7.text: reject the “spirits” and to keep to the ordinary life. This happens mostly in

8.text: the case of only children, because of the danger pertaining to the shamanistic

9.text: call, especially in the beginning. The protest of the parents is, however, of

10.text: no avail, because the rejection of the “spirits” is much more dangerous even

11.text: than the acceptance of their call. A young man thwarted in his call to

12.text: inspiration will either sicken and shortly die, or else the “spirits” will induce

13.text: him to renounce his home and go far away, where he may follow his vocation

15.text: On the other hand, it is entirely permissible to abandon shamanistic

16.text: performances at a more mature age, after several years of practice; and the
16.note: An ink blot obscures most of the word after 'and'; only a final 'e' survives unobscured at 4× magnification. Keyed 'the' on grammatical and width grounds (fits 'and the anger of the “spirits”...' on L17) but the letterforms themselves are not legible — flagged for adjudication.

17.text: anger of the “spirits” is not incurred by it. I met several persons who as-

18.text: serted that formerly they had been great shamans, but that now they had

19.text: given up most of their exercises. As reason for this, they gave illness, age,

20.text: or simply a decrease of their shamanistic power, which in the course of time

21.text: manifested itself. One said that because of illness he felt as if his arms

22.text: and legs were frozen, and that thereafter they did not thaw, so that he was

23.text: unable to “shake himself” well upon the drum. Another said that he and

24.text: his “spirits” became tired of each other. Most of the cases, probably, were
24.note: mz/ocr read the opening curly quote as 'e' (“espirits”); confirmed at 2× against the raster it is “spirits”.

25.text: simply the result of recovery from the nervous condition which had made the

26.text: persons in question fit subjects for the inspiration. While the shaman is

27.text: in possession of the inspiration, he must practise, and cannot hide his power.

28.text: Otherwise it will manifest itself in the form of bloody sweat or in a fit of

29.resolved: iteˊyun = i, t, e, U+02CA, y, u, n
29.note: Native form confirmed against lexicon lookup: 1-064 attests iteˊyun / Iteˊyun (“akin to epilepsy”), matching this reading. Footnote marker ² (U+00B2) follows the closing period, tight, per print.

30.text: There are parents who wish their child to answer the call. This happens

31.text: especially in families rich in children, with large herds, and with several tents

32.text: of their own. Such a family is not inclined to feel anxious about a possible

33.text: loss of one of its members. On the contrary, they are desirous of having a

34.text: shaman of their own, — made to order, so to speak, — a special solicitor

35.text: before the “spirits,” and a caretaker in all extraordinary casualties of life.

36.text: A shaman by the name of Teiˊñet, in the country near the Wolverene

36.note: Raised mark after 'Tei' is stress U+02CA (per §4), not an apostrophe; mz/ocr keyed it as an apostrophe.

39.text: that, he continued to feel “bashful” for several years. On days of ceremo-

41.text: Koryak found an important amulet on the bank of the river, but left it there from sheer fright. He became

42.text: very ill, and his illness was ascribed to the anger of the amulet. After a considerable lapse of time he came

43.text: back to look for the amulet, and at last carried it away with him.
